name: Setmelanotide
used_for: FDA-labeled (Imcivree) to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction in adults and children with acquired hypothalamic obesity (age 4 and older), Bardet-Biedl syndrome (age 2 and older), or POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency confirmed by genetic testing (age 2 and older). The label says it is not expected to work for other obesity, including common (polygenic) obesity or obesity from other genetic syndromes. It is a melanocortin 4 receptor agonist.

entries.text: Acquired hypothalamic obesity: labeled starting dosage 0.5 mg (0.05 mL) subcutaneously once daily for 2 weeks, then increased per the label titration tables.
entries.population: Adults and children aged 4 years and older with acquired hypothalamic obesity per the Imcivree label

entries.text: Bardet-Biedl syndrome or POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency: labeled starting dosage 2 mg subcutaneously once daily for 2 weeks (1 mg if not tolerated), with a labeled maintenance dosage of 3 mg once daily.
entries.population: Adults and children aged 12 years and older per the Imcivree label

entries.text: Bardet-Biedl syndrome or POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency: labeled starting dosage 1 mg subcutaneously once daily for 2 weeks, with a labeled maintenance dosage of 3 mg once daily; children aged 2 to under 6 start at 0.5 mg with weight-based titration.
entries.population: Children aged 6 to under 12 years per the Imcivree label

administration_guidance.text: Label: given once daily at the beginning of the day, without regard to meals.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Label: injected subcutaneously in the abdomen, thigh or arm, rotating to a different site each day.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Label: if a dose is missed, the once daily regimen resumes with the next scheduled dose.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Label: unopened vials are stored refrigerated (2 to 8 C), or may be kept at room temperature (up to 30 C) for up to 30 days; opened vials are discarded after 30 days or at expiration, whichever comes first.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Label: the vial is removed from the refrigerator about 15 minutes before injection, or warmed by rolling it gently between the palms for 60 seconds.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: Skin hyperpigmentation was the most common adverse reaction in the Bardet-Biedl syndrome trial (61% of participants, 23 of 38), with injection site erythema in 48%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the POMC and LEPR deficiency trials, injection site reactions occurred in every participant; nausea occurred in 5 of 10 (POMC) and 4 of 11 (LEPR) participants and vomiting in 3 of 10 (POMC). No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Label warnings and precautions: disturbance in sexual arousal, depression and suicidal ideation, hypersensitivity reactions, skin hyperpigmentation and nevi development, and (in acquired hypothalamic obesity) acute adrenal insufficiency and sodium imbalance.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: The Obesity Action Coalition describes Imcivree as a daily injection for obesity from POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency, cites trial results of 8 in 10 participants losing at least 10% of body weight, and says it is not for common obesity or unconfirmed genetic causes. The page predates label expansions to other conditions.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Imcivree (setmelanotide) (Rhythm Pharmaceuticals), published April 2026.
research.finding: Lists approved uses for acquired hypothalamic obesity, Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and POMC/PCSK1/LEPR deficiency, with once-daily subcutaneous dosing and explicit limits of use.

research.summary: Two single-arm open-label phase 3 trials of setmelanotide in 10 people with POMC deficiency and 11 with LEPR deficiency (Clement et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol).
research.finding: At about 1 year, 80% (POMC) and 45% (LEPR) lost at least 10% of body weight; hunger scores fell. Injection-site reactions and skin darkening were universal; nausea and vomiting were common. Very small, uncontrolled.

research.summary: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial of setmelanotide in 38 patients with Bardet-Biedl or Alstrom syndrome (Haqq et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol).
research.finding: 32.3% of Bardet-Biedl patients aged 12 and older reached at least 10% weight reduction at 52 weeks. Results were inconclusive for Alstrom syndrome. Skin hyperpigmentation (61%) and injection-site erythema (48%) were common.

research.summary: TRANSCEND: randomized placebo-controlled trial of setmelanotide in 120 people aged 4 to 66 with acquired hypothalamic obesity, 52 weeks (N Engl J Med).
research.finding: BMI changed -16.5% with setmelanotide versus +3.3% with placebo; hunger scores improved more. Serious adverse events occurred in 28% versus 8%; skin hyperpigmentation, nausea, vomiting and headache were common. Funded by Rhythm Pharmaceuticals.

dose.summary: The label starts with a 2 week low dose that depends on the condition and age, then increases to a maintenance dose, usually 3 mg once daily. No online source gave different doses.

cycle_length.summary: It is meant as ongoing treatment. Trials ran about 1 year, and the label describes a short placebo withdrawal followed by restarting treatment. The Obesity Action Coalition says weight increased when treatment was stopped.

items.text: The Bardet-Biedl syndrome trial ran 52 weeks, and 32.3% of participants aged 12 and older reached at least 10% weight reduction.
items.label: research

items.text: The POMC and LEPR deficiency trials followed participants for about 1 year, and 80% (POMC) and 45% (LEPR) lost at least 10% of body weight. These were very small, uncontrolled trials.
items.label: research

items.text: In the TRANSCEND trial of acquired hypothalamic obesity, treatment and placebo were compared over 52 weeks.
items.label: research

items.text: Label: in the POMC and LEPR deficiency trials, patients who had lost weight entered an 8-week double-blind withdrawal (4 weeks on treatment, 4 weeks on placebo), then restarted treatment for up to 32 weeks.
items.label: research

items.text: The Obesity Action Coalition says weight increased when treatment was stopped in trials and weight loss continued when treatment was restarted.

mechanism.summary: It activates the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R), a brain pathway that controls hunger and energy use, to reduce food intake and weight.

items.text: Label: setmelanotide is an MC4 receptor agonist. It re-establishes activity of the MC4 receptor pathway to reduce food intake and promote weight loss in people with certain genetic or hypothalamic causes of obesity.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: In the largest trial, people with acquired hypothalamic obesity had BMI change of -16.5% versus +3.3% on placebo at 52 weeks. In rare genetic obesity, small trials showed at least 10% weight loss in many participants. It is not expected to work for common obesity.
